CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Karanganyar Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of Regional Government Administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Karanganyar.
4. Regional Apparatus is the supporting element of the Regent in the administration of regional government consisting of Regional Secretariat, DPRD Secretariat, Regional Agencies, Regional Technical Institutions, Sub-districts and Urban Villages.
5. Implementation is the form of execution of protection for women and children victims of violence.
6. Protection of women and children victims of violence is every activity aimed at providing a sense of security for victims and protecting their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection, whether medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic or psychological protection from all forms of violence and discriminatory acts.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those still in the womb.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences suffering and or distress either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
9. Violence is any act that results in or can result in suffering or distress, whether physical, sexual, economic, social or psychological to the victim.
10. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT P2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
11. Commission for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as KP2A is a Commission that functions to formulate policy programs for the protection of women and children victims of violence with Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) and Child Rights Mainstreaming (PHA) strategies.
12. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims.
13. Social Community Institution is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) and or other community organizations.
14. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
15. Population is Indonesian citizens and/or foreigners who enter legally and reside in the territory of Indonesia.

Article I
(1) The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the KP2A framework.
(2) KP2A in handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological and economic protection, may establish partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.
(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms, as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands, or other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented according to standard operational procedures (SOP) which will be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

1.9.rationale: The original Indonesian text explicitly includes sexual exploitation within the definition of sexual violence. Pasal 10 ayat (3) states sexual violence includes “pemaksaan hubungan seksual dengan orang lain untuk tujuan komersial dan/atau tujuan tertentu” (forcing sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes), which is a form of sexual exploitation. This exact content was present in the retrieved English candidates ([1.9-16]). The judge was overly strict by requiring the policy to use the specific terms “sexual slavery” or “sexual exploitation,” even though the commercial-purpose forced sex clause substantively covers exploitation.

2.1.evaluator_rationale: The candidate sentences describe implementation at national and regional levels and involvement of community/social institutions, but do not indicate coordination or cooperation with governments across different jurisdictions (e.g., inter-regional, provincial-national coordination mechanisms).

GENERAL
The Government has the obligation to provide a sense of security and freedom for every citizen of its society from all forms of violence in the form of threats and actions that can disturb or damage psychological, physical, sexual and economic security, as mandated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution, which protects the entire nation and homeland of Indonesia.
The Indonesian Government has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of all forms of Discrimination against women, consequently the Indonesian Government must comply with these provisions. Likewise in the fourth amendment of the 1945 Constitution, Chapter XV of the 1945 Constitution concerning Human Rights, states that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the state, especially the Government.
To realize the achievement of enforcement and fulfillment of human rights, the government is obliged to provide protection and security for women and children as set forth in a policy both at the national and regional levels.
In the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women of 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as successors of the nation are creatures created by God Almighty, therefore they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be safeguarded properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class in social, national and state life.
From the series of policy provisions mentioned above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children both in the form of policies applicable at the national and regional levels.

5.2.rationale: The original Indonesian text only says implementation “harus memperhatikan norma-norma agama” (must pay attention to religious norms) (Pasal 8 ayat (3)). It does not describe engaging religious leaders/organizations as stakeholders, partners, or implementers. Membership elements for KP2A include “Tokoh Masyarakat” (community leaders) but not specifically religious institutions/leaders. Therefore the judge’s ‘No’ is consistent with the text; the golden ‘Yes’ appears to conflate ‘considering religious norms’ with ‘religious engagement’.

5.3.evaluator_rationale: While the policy mentions community participation and includes “community leaders” as an element of KP2A membership, it does not explicitly or implicitly specify collaboration with traditional/cultural organizations or leaders.
